checkpoints.description: [1/2] Two follow-ups from re-verifying my own proposals: (1) the perf recorder measured one process and called it a baseline, so a recording is now 5 passes reduced to a median plus MAD and a gate run is 3 passes, with a metric failing only past 1.5x AND median+6 MADs; commitP95 budget raised 5 -> 10 ms on instruction. (2) A resumed run could not see its tool results: appendMessage now accepts a tool role written without a text.ended event, listMessages excludes tool rows unless asked, and rebuildMessages carries them through.

impact_assessment.why: The perf baseline described a different host (pristine tree failed it too) and a resumed conversation repeated work it had already done, so neither number nor behaviour could be trusted.
impact_assessment.benefits: A timing claim now comes with its spread, so a busy machine is visible instead of silently failing; and work resumed in a conversation continues instead of restarting blind.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: agent-perf baseline schema 1 -> 2, and listMessages default shape; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: tool rows are durable state the UI does not render
impact_assessment.mitigation: A schema-1 baseline still reads through its metrics key; tool rows are excluded by default so every existing reader is byte-for-byte unchanged; both proven by the 638-test suite and 12/12 gates

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Fix the measured prompt-test flake: the test asserted a bare 'L5' against a prompt that embeds a mkdtemp path whose random suffix contains L5 in 0.4% of samples, so it failed about once in 250 full-suite runs for a reason unrelated to imports. Both assertions now name the whole line.

impact_assessment.why: A gate that fails at random teaches everyone to re-run it rather than read it, which is worse than the bug it hides.
impact_assessment.benefits: The prompt test now fails only when the import depth behaviour actually changes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the assertion is stricter, not looser; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: MAX_IMPORT_DEPTH is 3 and verified, so 'L3 inlined, its own @l4 plain' remains the behaviour under test; the full suite is green.

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Wave 3b: server/shellTasks.ts gives bash a real background mode. run_in_background starts a detached child, writes its output to a log under the state home, and returns a task id and log path; shell_output, shell_tasks and kill_shell read, list and stop it. The pre-existing killProcessTree teardown is reused, every task dies with the server, and a 30-minute lifetime bounds a task nobody stops.

impact_assessment.why: Every command blocked the agent loop, so a build or a watch occupied a whole step and the delegate tool's background flag was declared but never read.
impact_assessment.benefits: A long command no longer costs the run its remaining steps, and its output lands in a file the agent can read a window of instead of flooding the context.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: three new tool names enter the harness profile; dependency: none; concurrency: a registry shared across runs in one process; state: log files under the state home
impact_assessment.mitigation: The registry is capped at 40 tasks, every task is killed on server stop, kill reuses the tested process-tree teardown, and 6 tests drive start/read/offset/list/kill/refusal

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Two measured defects fixed. (1) A background task's log had no ceiling: a loop printing 24-byte lines wrote 2888895 bytes in 3s. It now stops at 1 MB, marks the task truncated, and says so when read. (2) readTaskOutput loaded the whole log to return a 200-char window (19.41ms on that log); it now seeks with readSync and allocates only the window (5.23ms after). Also removed delegate's background parameter, which the implementation never read, and added a mutation-tested audit that fails when any tool advertises a parameter nothing reads.

impact_assessment.why: Both defects were in code I shipped in the previous turn, found by re-reading my own work rather than by trusting it.
impact_assessment.benefits: A runaway command can no longer fill the state directory, reading a large log is bounded, and a schema can no longer lie about a capability.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: readTaskOutput now reports truncated when a log hit the ceiling; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: logs are capped, which is the intent
impact_assessment.mitigation: Both fixes are pinned by tests that assert the ceiling and the seek cost; the schema audit was verified by reintroducing the dead parameter and watching it fail

checkpoints.description: [1/1] Bound the read ledger's second cache. LEDGERS was capped at 32 runs but HASHES, keyed by absolute path, was not: measured at 833 bytes retained per hashed path with no way to release it, so a long-lived server walking a large repository accumulates forever. HASHES now clears at 4096 entries; a clear costs one re-read per file rather than a wrong answer. The ceiling is injectable so the test proves it with 40 files in 120ms instead of 4096 files in 8.5s.

impact_assessment.why: The ledger is the guard against blind writes; an unbounded guard that slowly eats the process is its own defect.
impact_assessment.benefits: A long session cannot grow this map without bound, and the cache still answers identically after a clear.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none exported beyond test helpers; dependency: none; concurrency: a clear during a run costs a re-hash, not a wrong answer; state: in-memory only
impact_assessment.mitigation: The cap is mutation-tested (removing it fails with 'expected 11 to be less than or equal to 10'), and correctness after a clear is asserted by hashing the same file before and after
